rounds.text: Oneindig Technologies Ltd presents a concerning financial profile characterized by aggressive leverage and a complete disconnect between reported profits and actual cash generation. While the company reports strong accounting returns, its cash conversion is deeply negative at -1.71x, with operating cash flow plummeting to Rs -10.43 Cr and free cash flow to Rs -33.24 Cr in March 2026 [E18, E19, E20]. This liquidity strain is compounded by a dangerous surge in borrowings from Rs 6.96 Cr to Rs 46.32 Cr, pushing the debt-to-equity ratio to 2.23x, which indicates that debt now exceeds net worth [E22, E24]. Furthermore, the company struggles with operational efficiency, evidenced by high debtors of 154 days and inconsistent operating margins over the last two years [E16, E17, E36]. Valuation concerns are underscored by a negative margin of safety, as the current market price exceeds the intrinsic value derived from a discounted cash flow analysis [E30, E31]. Conceded: the company demonstrates high profitability metrics, including an ROE of 34.4%, an ROCE of 27.0%, and significant compounded sales growth of 54% [E11, E12, E13]. However, these figures appear unsustainable given the underlying cash flow deficits and the thin buffer provided by a 1.47x current ratio [E23].
